answer.rationale: Write-path p99 has degraded since shortly after a release, making rollback the most directly implicated fix (b1: rollback cleared a prior checkout error spike cleanly). Regional failover is explicitly contraindicated right now because writes are hot and heavy settlement traffic is in flight (b2: failover during hot writes caused a 40-minute replication gap and lost writes) — that risk is unacceptable given the availability-without-losing-writes objective. I'm verifying b1 and b2 specifically because they bear directly on which action is safe versus which is memory-flagged dangerous under current write load. Rather than a full rollback of the release across all traffic, I'm scoping this as a small guarded rollback/canary-reversal first: the 90-minute climb slightly predates a clean two-hour-old release correlation, so causality isn't fully certain, and settlement peak load could itself be a contributing factor to the latency rather than the release alone. A guarded rollback lets me observe whether write-path p99 recovers without committing irreversibly during peak settlement volume, preserving the option to pivot to capacity or circuit-breaker responses if rollback doesn't resolve it.
